General/Typical Procedure: Representative Procedure for the Synthesis of Di-O-acyl-glyceramides. Compound 20b. A mixture of acetic acid (57 µL, 1.0 mmol) and Cu(acac)2 (2.6 mg, 0.01 mmol, 1 mol %) toluene (2 mL) in a 10 mL round-bottom flask was heated to 60 °C for 10 min under nitrogen. To it was added dropwise a solution of diazoketone 1a (226 mg, 1.3 mmol, 1.3 equiv) in toluene (2 mL).Once gas evolution was judged complete, the reaction mixture was stirred an additional 5 min, then cooled and concentrated in Vacuo. The oily residue was blanketed in nitrogen, then treated with isobutyric acid (140 µL, 1.5 mmol, 1.5 equiv) and t-BuNC (170 µL, 1.5 mmol, 1.5 equiv). The resulting reaction mixture was stirred at rt under N2 for 20 h. The product was purified by silica gel flash column chromatography (1:1 EtOAc:hexanes, Rf ) 0.3) to afford 5b (338 mg, 90%) as a pale-yellow oil.

experimental_procedure: Representative Procedure for Ugi Reactions of Convertible Isonitrile 7 Primary amine 12 (10.5 mmol) and oxo compound 13 (10.5 mmol) were dissolved in MeOH (20 mL) in the presence of Na2SO4 (5.30 g) and stirred for 2 h at r.t. to preform the imine. Subsequently, carboxylic acid 11 (10.46 mmol) and convertible isonitrile 7 (2.00 g, 10.46 mmol) were added and the mixture was stirred overnight. When TLC monitoring (CH2Cl2-MeOH, 19:1) indicated complete formation of the Ugi reaction products, the mixture was evaporated to dryness under reduced pressure. The residue was either used directly for the next step, or dissolved in EtOAc (50 mL) and H2O (30 mL). In the latter case, the water layer was discarded and the organic layer was washed with citric acid solution (3 × 30 mL, pH 2), H2O (2 × 30 mL), sat. NaHCO3 solution (3 × 30 mL), and finally with brine (3 × 30 mL). The organic solvent was dried over Na2SO4, filtered, and evaporated to give the crude Ugi reaction products. The α-aminoacyl amide derivatives are formed in yields ranging from 51-90%. yield 90%.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of the Passerini adducts: general procedure. The appropriate arylglyoxal or glyoxylamide (1 or 6) (5mmol) was suspended in diethyl ether (5mL). Acetic acid (3, 5mmol), and the corresponding isocyanide (2) (5mmol) were successively added, and the mixture was stirred 48-72 h at room temperature. In the case of using arylglyoxals (1), an abundant precipitate was formed, which was filtered and successively washed with i-PrOH and i-Pr2O, yielding a product (4) usually pure enough to be used in the following reaction. In the case of using glyoxylamides (6, R1 = NHR or NRR') or glyoxylic esters (6, R1= OR), the reaction mixture was extracted with CH2Cl2 (4 × 10mL),and the organic phase was dried with Na2SO4 and concentrated in the rotatory evaporator. The residue was purified by flash column chromatography(Φ = 3, L = 12cm;hexane/EtOAc from 7:3 to 3:7), giving the corresponding product (7). In the case of 7e, a precipitate forms, which is filtered, and washed with i-PrOH and i-Pr2O, yielding the product usually pure enough to be used in the following reaction. For analytical purposes, the adducts 4 and 7e were further purified by recrystallisation from ethanol. Compound 7b, Yield: 70%.
